content.text: Changan, I just brought Xingren back from the hospital, and the diagnosis results are out.
How is it? What did the doctor say?
It's a mild allergy, and the doctor said it might be related to allergens, such as dust mites in the environment or certain foods.
Oh, that sounds somewhat similar to what we previously discussed about seasonal changes or stress, but more specific. Did the doctor provide a treatment plan?
Well, this is the plan given by the doctor. I'll send it to you for a look.
Received. It looks quite detailed.
The medication primarily consists of antihistamines, and environmental measures include regular cleaning and avoiding certain foods. Do you think this plan is feasible?
From a practical standpoint, it seems quite reasonable. However, the implementation might be a bit cumbersome, such as the frequency of cleaning and the dosage of medication.
I think the same way. When work gets busy, I worry I won't be able to take care of everything. I'm really grateful that you helped take Xingren to the hospital, and now I have to trouble you again.
You're welcome, friends help each other out. I suggest making a plan to systematize the treatment process, which will save both worry and effort.
Great idea! The automation solution you mentioned earlier can come in handy this time.
Yes, I made a reference tracking sheet and sent it to you. It can record the severity of itching, medication usage, and so on.
Wow, this table is really practical! It looks like the style of the computer usage report you shared before—simple and clear.
Well, I'm used to managing things with tables; it's efficient. You can adjust the content based on the doctor's plan.
Thank you! However, veterinary care for pets is really not cheap. This check-up and medication cost quite a bit, and I still need to keep an eye on things, which feels quite stressful.
Understanding, just like when we last complained about health issues, raising pets also requires balancing investment. But knowing the reason is always better than worrying blindly.

Yes, at least we know it's an allergy, not something more serious. This reminds me of the last time we made plans to eat out, and you recommended a restaurant with great value for money. Now I need to find a balance in pet care too.
Yes, pragmatism. We can brainstorm ways to optimize Almond's living environment together, such as using automated cleaning equipment to reduce manual intervention.
Okay, I'll look into it later. Thanks to your help this time, from diagnosis to planning, you've saved me a lot of trouble.
No problem, we support each other. Now that the treatment direction is clear, the next step is to carry it out. Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.
